why: THE FACTORY'S OWN HEARTBEAT, and until 2026-09-12 nothing had one. The pulse belt is universal state - one file, at the factory root, written by the one machine that owns it - and the machine has been built, gated and in CI since `The pulse is universal state, not repo state (#2)`. It had never executed. Not once. `.refer-factory/pulse-belt.jsonl` did not exist, because this repo declared eighteen machines and zero triggers, so universal state had nothing universal writing it. Operator, 2026-09-12: 'why i'm not seeing the pulse on the belt on incoming and resolved' - the answer was that there was no belt, and the reason the question was hard to chase is that `npm run gate:pulse-belt` passes honestly against throwaway fixtures. The machine works. Nothing ran it. A machine nothing declares is invisible rather than broken, which is the failure shape `triggers.cjs` names in its own header as the one this factory exists to remove. DECLARED HERE, BESIDE THIS REPO'S OWN MACHINERY, AND NOT IN machines/ - that directory is one copy for every repo, so a trigger in it would ship this repo's cadence to all of them. The machine is universal, the cadence is local; this file is the local half. EVERY MUST STAY 5m, and this is the trap. pulse-belt.cjs line 208 breaks out of its search the moment it finds a trigger whose id is `pulse-belt` - 'our own declaration wins over the tick's' - so this `every` sets the STAGE LENGTH, not merely how often the machine is invoked. Run it every 15m while declaring 5m and the board draws a cycle that disagrees with the clock that made it, which the machine's own header calls a display that lies. It is also exactly the collision that forced the `pulse` -> `pulse-check` rename on the same day: two different things wearing one name, on two different clocks. Three stages at 5m means a card is visible for 15 minutes total - incoming, then belt, then resolved - so a single run only ever shows beat 1 with belt and resolved empty, and that is correct rather than broken. NOTHING DRIVES THIS YET, which is why `driverPending` is set rather than `drivenBy`. The only engine on this host is the `LivingFactory-Schedule` task, and it cannot be pointed here: `schedule.cjs` line 86 is `path.resolve(__dirname, '../..')`, so it resolves its subject from its own location and drives Telechurch no matter what working directory it is launched with. Changing that task's Start In would do nothing at all. The driver this needs is a CLOCK rather than an engine - a scheduled task running `node machines/pulse-belt.cjs` in this directory every 5 minutes - and the pulse doctrine in `pulse.trigger.json` demands exactly that: 'deliberately the stupidest component in the factory: one tool, no judgement, nothing that can prompt', because a thing whose only job is to prove time passed must never have a reason to hesitate. Registering that task was refused by the host's permission classifier on 2026-09-12 and is awaiting the operator. Until it exists this declaration is still doing work: it is what lets the machine say GAP - 'the cycle is not being driven on time' - instead of reporting beat 1 as though beat 1 were healthy.
